messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Fwd: Problems with RSTAN install
parts:
Downgrading R is never really the answer. It is just a matter of getting everything aligned. The first thing to try seems to be reinstalling Rcpp from source with

install.packages(c("Rcpp", "inline"), type = "source")

If that is insufficient to get rstan working, then should do a

remove.packages("rstan")

and then install rstan again. If you are using the latest version of the Mac operating system, then I think you have to install rstan with CXX=g++ in ~/.R/Makevars and then change it to CXX=clang++ when you want to run models.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Fwd: Problems with RSTAN install
parts:
Hey all,

I just wanted to alert the list that I just installed RStan on a new Mac (Mavericks, latest Xcode) and had a similar problem to Fredrik and Sam compiling the 8 schools code . I followed the instructions on the RStan Getting Started page and had R crash on me when I tried to run the 8 schools example. I followed Ben's instructions above to reinstall Rcpp and inline (copy/pasted Ben's above into the R console) from source, and the 8 schools code now runs fine. Given that a few other users have had similar problems, I wonder if there is a versioning issue with what R installs when install.packages(c('Rcpp','inline')) is called vs. install.packages(c('Rcpp', 'inline'), type = 'source').

Rob

messages.author: 3f22b207863d2049
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Fwd: Problems with RSTAN install
parts:
Hi Michael,

You need to find the file "Makevars" that is in the folder ~/.R/ (where "~" is something like usr/[username]). ".R" starts with a period, so this indicates it is a hidden folder. You can't find it with finder, unless you do some tweaks. See here how to do that.

Btw, I recently got a new Macbook Pro, and I was able to successfully install rstan with CXX=clang++ in my Makevars file (and having installed inline and Rcpp from source).

Luc
